**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Wheat leaf blade — narrow, elongated
- **Color pattern:** The leaf is predominantly tan/straw-yellow, with a distinct darker central stripe/streak running the full length parallel to the midvein
- **Texture/pattern:** Long, linear lesion along the leaf axis; the upper tip retains a bit of green while the bulk of the tissue is bleached/necrotic
- **Key features:** Full-length pale stripes coalescing to give a straw/bleached appearance — no discrete pustule rows (ruling out Stripe Rust), no oval lesions with yellow halos (ruling out Tan Spot)

**Reasoning through candidates:**

| Disease | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Cephalosporium Stripe** | Strong match — pale yellow-to-straw stripes run full leaf length, tissue bleaches to straw/tan |
| Stripe Rust | Would show orange-yellow pustule rows, not smooth bleached stripes |
| Bacterial Leaf Streak | Water-soaked, more translucent narrow streaks, often with bacterial exudate |
| Tan Spot | Oval/diamond tan lesions with yellow halo, not full-length stripes |
| Barley Yellow Dwarf Virus | Tip/marginal yellowing, not a central longitudinal stripe |

The dominant feature — a long, pale straw-colored stripe running the full leaf length with the surrounding tissue also bleaching — is the textbook presentation of **Cephalosporium Stripe**, caused by *Cephalosporium gramineum* (now *Hymenula cerealis*). The fungus invades vascular tissue and disrupts water/nutrient transport, producing exactly this kind of longitudinal chlorotic-to-necrotic striping.
